title: Retain matmul sorted-key boundary after reverse-encounter audit

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Audit whether the remaining sorted(row_result) boundary in TypedRelationBlock.matmul can be deleted without introducing a second accumulator, ordering flag, alternate constructor, backend or execution path. Preserve canonical CSR column ordering, semiring accumulation, operation limits, entry bounds and exact Fourfold subject/axis contracts.

audit.finding: The sort is semantically required. row_result insertion order follows first contraction encounter order: left-row middle indices are canonical, and each right-row span is canonical, but columns emitted by different middle rows are not globally monotone. A valid contraction can therefore encounter a larger target column before a smaller one.
audit.counterexample: For one source row connected to middle labels m1 then m2, let right row m1 reach target B (column 1) and right row m2 reach target A (column 0). The accumulator inserts columns in order 1,0 although the output CSR contract requires 0,1. Removing sorted(row_result) would either construct a non-canonical block rejected by the direct constructor or require a new ordered accumulator/merge abstraction.
audit.semiring_independence: The ordering requirement is structural and does not depend on Boolean, natural, tropical or evidence-dag scalar semantics. Semiring operations determine the value stored per target column, not the global first-encounter ordering of distinct target columns.
audit.gardener_conclusion: Retain one row-local sorted-key transient as the minimal existing deterministic boundary. Do not replace it with an ordered accumulator, heap/merge layer, ordering flag or alternate matmul path merely to delete the sort. Pin the counterexample in the existing contraction test owner so future gardening cannot silently remove the boundary.

test_change.purpose: Construct a contraction whose valid encounter order is target column 1 then 0 and assert that the canonical result is emitted as column_indices (0, 1) and iter_entries A then B.

semantic_invariants.csr_order: TypedRelationBlock output columns remain strictly increasing inside each row; the existing sorted(row_result) is retained as the canonicalization boundary.
semantic_invariants.semiring: Boolean, natural, tropical and evidence-dag multiplication/addition behavior is unchanged; no production code changed.
semantic_invariants.operation_budget: The existing exact contraction operation counter and refusal point are unchanged.
semantic_invariants.entry_bound: The existing len(values) + len(row_result) > MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES refusal remains unchanged and still executes before sorting/emitting the row.
semantic_invariants.axes_and_subject: Typed middle-axis compatibility, exact Fourfold subject identity and output signature/axes are unchanged.
semantic_invariants.source_of_truth: KnowledgeForest/Fourfold remain authoritative; TypedRelationBlock remains a regenerable internal computational view.
semantic_invariants.public_api: No public API, wire schema, benchmark schema, authority or promotion contract changes.

result.summary: GPU-92 proves that matmul contraction encounter order is not a global target-column ordering guarantee. The existing row-local sorted-key boundary is therefore retained, and a focused regression test now pins the reverse-encounter counterexample without changing production code.
